30 Days of Vibe Coding | Day 28: Week 4 Wrap-Up — How to Save Tokens in Claude Code
Well... we've made it to Week 4, the final week, which also makes this the last wrap-up of the whole series.
For this wrap-up, let's talk about usage limits.
If you've been Vibe Coding along this whole time, you've probably run into the usage limit more than a few times by now. So this post is all about that.

Quick bit of background first: on the Pro and Max plans, your usage is shared between chatting on claude.ai and Claude Code. And there are two kinds of limits: a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit.
First, how does your usage get eaten up?
After everything we've covered, I'm sure you know by now that the biggest catch with AI is the Token limit, and how many Tokens you burn mainly comes down to the size of the "Context."
The key point fits in one sentence:
Context is everything on the table. The more stuff there is, the more Tokens each round uses, and the more it costs.
Most of the Context gets taken up by these:

: This is the big one. Remember the table I used as an example back on Day 6? Basically, every time the AI replies to you, it has to look over the entire Context Window (the tabletop) again, so the longer you chat, the more Tokens you spend.
Files it reads and command output
: Every file the AI reads and every
it runs, all that content and those results go into the Context, and they get read again on the next round.
: It's loaded automatically every time you start a new conversation, including the file we pulled in with
on Day 17. So the fatter it gets, the more every round costs. The official docs also recommend keeping CLAUDE.md under 200 lines.

: From my teaching experience, a lot of Vibe Coding beginners tend to install a whole pile of Skills. But every installed Skill keeps its description sitting on the table the whole time, and the body of any Skill that's been called stays in the conversation until you
: MCP tool names are always on the table, but that part's pretty small. What really takes up space is after one gets triggered, when MCP dumps whatever it found into the Context.
: As we covered on Day 19, a subagent has its own Context Window, so it doesn't get mixed into your main conversation. But every subagent you spin up still has its Context counted toward your usage.

So you'll notice a lot of Token usage happens without you even realizing it. You might just want to look something up in the docs, run a test, or add a Skill, and before you know it the table's gotten pretty bloated.
That's also why I suggested right from the start that you begin with the $20 subscription. That's how you find out how much usage you actually need, without wasting a bunch of money.
It's actually pretty simple. Just stick to a few big principles:
The smaller the Context, the less you spend
when you're done. Don't leave everything sitting on the table.
Don't pile on external tools (MCP, Skills)
: If you don't need an external tool, don't install it. They stay on the table eating Context the whole time. It might not be much, but if one gets triggered by accident, it can eat a ton.
: For big changes, run Plan Mode first. Heading in the wrong direction and having to redo everything is the most expensive thing there is.

Fun fact: someone on the Claude Code team once said publicly that AI is smart enough now that you don't really need to lean on Plan Mode anymore (though they also said Plan Mode isn't going away). Still, I think it's really useful, because it lets you check the direction before a big change and avoid redoing work.
Same as the first three weeks, here's a checklist for the wrap-up. Go through it line by line and see whether you've actually done each one:
The project has at least one Hook set up (Day 22)
The core money-calculation logic has tests, and you've made them fail and then pass again (Day 23)
Used Plan Mode to take stock of all the tech debt (Day 24)
Did one post-launch update, changing SPEC first before touching anything (Day 26)
Every addition and edit branches off develop, goes through a PR, and you've fixed things based on CodeRabbit's suggestions (Day 27)

We're about at the end, so here's a quick summary:
Pro and Max usage is shared between claude.ai chat and Claude Code, and the limits come in two kinds: a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit.

Token usage mainly comes down to the size of the Context. Chat history, files it reads and command output, CLAUDE.md, Skills, MCP, and subagents all eat into your usage, and a lot of it happens without you noticing.
Saving usage comes down to three principles:
when you're done to keep the Context as small as possible, don't pile on MCP servers and Skills you don't use, and run Plan Mode before big changes so you don't have to redo work.
Start with the $20 plan, get a feel for how much usage you really need, then decide whether to upgrade.
